10.text: The next missionaries — probably owing to the unhappy episode told

11.text: above — were selected among the monks. Their number gradually increased.

12.text: At the close of the nineteenth century three of them were already on the

13.text: Kolyma, — one as head of the mission in Nishne-Kolymsk; another in

14.text: the village Piatistennoye, on the Large Anui River; and the third in the

15.text: Yakut settlement Sen-quel, on the outskirts of the western tundra. The place

16.text: for this missionary was selected personally by the Bishop of Yakutsk, Dionisius;

17.text: and it was to be on the Big Chukchee River, in the middle of the desert.

18.text: The bishop says in his order, “The very name of the river shows that this

19.text: place has served from ancient times as a habitation of the Chukchee.” Bishop
19.note: Closing quote is curly U+201D per §1/R1; machine draft had straight U+0022.

20.text: Dionisius evidently wanted by his order to solve the ethnographic problem of

21.text: the Big Chukchee River, which has not yet been solved by scientists. The

22.text: place has really served as a habitation in times far remote, but serves no

23.text: longer as such. Since the country about the Big Chukchee River is so

24.text: thoroughly a desert, the new missionary had to remain on the outskirts of

25.text: the tundra, in one of the outlying Yakut settlements.

26.text: At the present time the Kolyma country has seven priests, with a corre-

27.text: sponding number of churchmen, — four with parishes, and three Chukchee

28.text: missionaries. For a Christian population of about four thousand, including

29.text: the baptized Chukchee, this number is perhaps a little too large. Verkhne-

30.text: Kolymsk, Sredne-Kolymsk, and Nishne-Kolymsk have wooden churches. Other

31.text: villages have only rough wooden chapels, where services are held once or

32.text: twice a year by the priest, who comes for the purpose. Plate XXXV, Fig. 3,

37.text: Incidentally I will mention only one fact. In the eighties of the nineteenth

38.text: century there was in the province of Yakutsk one single priest of pure Yakut

39.text: blood, newly ordained at that time. Now, in the whole province of Yakutsk

40.text: there is a single parish, where the inhabitants do not know anything of the

41.text: Yakut language, and rather despise the Yakut national element. This parish

42.text: is Nishne-Kolymsk. The single Yakut priest was appointed to the single
